chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who touches a carcass: should he perform ghusl because of it? He said: “No; that applies only to the human being alone.”

key_terms.يَمَسُّ: touches or comes into contact with
key_terms.ٱلْإِنْسَانِ: the human being, specified here as the case to which the ruling applies
key_terms.ٱلْمَيْتَةَ: a carcass or dead animal body

ai.seo_question: Does touching a dead animal require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity after touching a dead body. Imam Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that ghusl is not required for touching a carcass, and that this ruling applies specifically to the human dead body alone.
